sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Hart County
sections.html:
Hart County is lake country in the northeast corner of Georgia, right beside I-85, with Hartwell as the county seat. Population is 28,639 as of 2025. Lake Hartwell drives much of the local market, so a shoreline lot, a farmhouse and a Hartwell bungalow can each raise different tax questions, from acreage covenants to homestead.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: P.O. Box 810, Hartwell, GA 30643, 706-376-3997. Values property, takes homestead applications and handles appeals.
  • Tax Commissioner: in the courthouse in Hartwell. Collects property tax, auto tags, timber payments, mobile home tax and the intangible recording tax.
  • Records: the county website links to a property tax record search and to an online payment site.

Have your parcel number handy before you call either office.

Rural parcels near the lake often combine a house with several acres, so ask whether the land carries any special assessment before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

Hart County property tax calendar
TaskDate
Returns and homestead filingJanuary 1 through April 1
Assessment notices mailedBy April 15
Appeal of a changed valueWithin 45 days of the notice date
Mobile home return and location permitJanuary 1 through May 1
Property tax bill due, normal yearDecember 20

Statewide, December 20 is the default due date. Counties may pick December 1 or November 15 instead. No interest runs until 60 days past the postmark. Your statement's printed date controls, so look there first, then pay by it.

Penalties can attach to delinquent taxes on top of interest. The Tax Commissioner has added a drop box outside the courthouse for property and auto payments, and an online payment option is linked from the county website.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. A mobile home standing in Hart on January 1 must be returned to the Tax Commissioner by May 1, and the yearly location permit window runs January 1 to May 1 as well. A newly placed home needs a permit within 30 days. Ask the Tax Commissioner when the tax on a mobile home account falls due.

If you cannot make the courthouse during the day, the drop box takes property and auto payments outside business hours. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Hart County assessment
sections.html:
Your written appeal has to carry a postmark within 45 days of the date on the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. That notice goes out when they disagree with the value you returned.

The county reviews every parcel annually and mails a notice by April 15. Owners in Hartwell and on the lake shore should read that notice as soon as it arrives, because the 45 day clock starts from the notice date. The assessors' office will explain the filing procedure by phone.

Another route runs through the return. You can file a return with the assessors from January 1 through April 1. If you think your value is too high, file a return reducing it by April 1 to have a chance at a lower value for next year's taxes. Tax that was wrongly or illegally collected can be claimed back within three years of payment, with a written claim to the county governing authority.

The homestead filer must live in the house as a legal residence, and the paperwork goes to the assessors' office. A person away for health reasons will not be denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office on their behalf.

  • Owning the property on January 1 and filing by the April 1 return date secures the exemption for that tax year.
  • Certain elderly owners qualify for additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead. Eligible owners should apply by April 1 so the benefit carries into later years.
  • Call the assessors at 706-376-3997 to ask whether a local homestead exemption sits on top of the state ones for your parcel.

In the year of a sale, remember that an exemption belongs to a person at an address. Your old filing stays behind when you leave, and a buyer who moves in after New Year's must file fresh. Skip the form and that year's relief is gone.

Elderly owners should ask the assessors which extra exemption forms apply to their age before April 1 arrives, since a missed deadline pushes the benefit to the following year.

Hart County is affordable by Georgia standards. For 2020 to 2024 the middle owned home is $215,100, the middle rent is $844 and 77.8% of homes are occupied by their owners. Median household income is $59,385.

The county counts 13,800 housing units against 11,034 households, and 197 building permits were issued in 2025. Population rose 10.9% from the April 2020 base to the 2025 estimate. Owners of a house that sits empty part of the year should ask both offices whether an exemption they hold still applies.

sections.h2: Before you list: a Hart County checklist
sections.html:
Missing paperwork causes more trouble than the tax itself. Run through these items a few weeks ahead of listing day.

  1. Pull your latest assessment notice and compare the value to what you think the house would sell for.
  2. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the unpaid balance, if any, and for the status of this year's bill.
  3. Confirm with the assessors that your homestead exemption is on file, and tell your buyer to file their own.
  4. If the property is a mobile home, locate the location permit and the return you filed.
  5. Look for any acreage or covenant paperwork that a buyer will ask about.

With those five items in a folder, your closing attorney can quote a payoff in a single call and your buyer's title company has less to chase. A cash buyer can often close quickly, so having the folder ready early keeps the tax balance from becoming the last open item.

The Tax Commissioner collects the intangible recording tax. A lender holding a long-term note on real estate has 90 days to record the security instrument locally. The charge is $1.50 per $500 of the note, rounded up for any fraction. A cash purchase has no note, so that charge does not arise.

For sellers the main items are a tax payoff figure and clear title. The Clerk of Superior Court handles recording at 185 West Franklin Street in Hartwell.

Before listing a Hart County house, gather your latest assessment notice, the most recent tax bill, any mobile home permit records and any covenant paperwork. Get the unpaid balance from the Tax Commissioner, then settle with the closing attorney which party carries this year's bill. If the house is a mobile home, bring the permit record so the buyer can see the location permit is current.

faqs.q: When are Hart County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 is the normal deadline, and state law holds off interest for 60 days after mailing. Go by the date on your bill.

faqs.q: How soon must a Hart County appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Postmark it within 45 days of the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. Phone 706-376-3997 for the steps.

faqs.q: When is the Hart County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. You need to have owned and lived in the house on January 1, with the form at the assessors' office by the return deadline.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Hart County mobile home tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Tax Commissioner. The return and the yearly location permit both fall between January 1 and May 1, and whoever owned the home there on January 1 files.

faqs.q: Does Hart County reassess every year?
faqs.a: Yes. Every parcel is reevaluated each year and notices go out by April 15, with 45 days to appeal a value you dispute.
